newsitem.title: USA: Energy Search ups reserves value sharply.
newsitem.headline: Energy Search ups reserves value sharply.

text.p: Energy Search, Inc, a small exploration company traded on the NASDAQ since last January, has had a remarkable record of successful gas finds in the Appalachian Basin, in West Virginia.

The company said in a statement on Monday that it "has drilled 13 consecutive successful natural gas wells on its Beaver project in Raleigh County of southern West Virginia," with the result that the value of the company's reserves at the end of the first quarter were 25 percent higher than year end 1996 at more than $26.8 million.
"This is the kind of success rate, 13 out of 13, when you start pinching yourself," said Charles Torrey, Chief Executive Officer of Energy Search in a telephone interview.

"The average estimated ultimate recoverable reserves of the 13 wells drilled to date is 484 million cubic feet (MMCF) per well, or 49% higher than the targeted estimate of 325 MMCF per well," Torrey said.

The gas is all "dry," with no associated liquids, which means the recovery costs are around 40 cents per thousand cubic foot, compared with a financial target of 75 cents when the company's stock was launched and around $1.10 per mcf for other producers in the area.

The gas has a slightly-above-normal British Termal Units content, which means it achieves a premium on the open market, which is among the more expensive in the country in the Appalachian region, Torrey said.
